notes: NEW in v5. About 16:30 on 13 June, sixty tanks of CCA with 29th Division infantry counterattacked southwest from Carentan and drove back the 17th SS attack (four German tanks lost) (Wikipedia Bloody Gulch). CMH ch. IX footnote: CCA was still attached to the 101st Airborne Division. Combat commands are treated as battle-group-size units. Commander not verified. Claim moved out of C0100, which was about the whole 2nd Armored Division.

current_activity: passing from VII Corps to XIX Corps control at noon
notes: Event date: Breakout-15 p296: at noon on 28 July Corlett's XIX Corps assumed responsibility for CCA of the 2nd Armored Division, reinforced by the 4th Division's 22nd Infantry, in the corps' new zone; Breakout-16 p304 says CCA and the 30th Division had been transferred from VII to XIX Corps. Event definition: a combat command of the 2nd Armored Division passes temporarily to XIX Corps while the rest of the division (less CCA) stays under VII Corps; this is a different relationship from the whole-division moves in C0509 and C0511. Relationship: unspecified_subordination to XIX Corps (the text says transferred); organic to the 2nd Armored Division. The end of the temporary arrangement is not documented as a date for CCA; the whole division is under XIX Corps by 2 August (C0226). Location: Breakout-15 p296 has CCA in possession of its Cobra objective, Le Mesnil-Herman, and probing toward Villebaudon and Tessy-sur-Vire at noon on 28 July; the point is the village centroid. The 22nd Infantry was attached to CCA. Breakout-15 p302: for the attack of 1 August Corlett attached CCA to the 29th Division, so CCA was still under XIX Corps on 31 July. Commander not verified. Event support: high (Green Book, noon 28 July). Location support: moderate (village named in the text, centroid).
